title: A nonzero vector of a vector space is not killed by some linear form
statement: Let $F$ be a field, $V$ an $F$-vector space and $v\in V$ with $v\ne0$. Then there is an $F$-linear map $\varphi:V\to F$ with $\varphi(v)\ne0$.

source.place: used without proof in More on Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 07PH (lemma-find-D): 'Thus we can choose a K'-derivation D' : L -> L with D'(f) != 0' (a nonzero element of the L-vector space Omega_{L/K'} and the universal property of differentials)
